memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "About Benjamin he said: 'Let the beloved of the Lord rest secure in him, for he shields him all day long, and the one the Lord loves rests between his shoulders.'" — Deut 33:12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
What a tender blessing for the tribe of Benjamin: "Let the beloved of the Lord rest secure in him... the one the Lord loves rests between his shoulders." This is one of the most intimate pictures of God's care in all of Scripture. To rest "between his shoulders" evokes the image of a beloved child carried close, perhaps on a father's back or held against his chest — safe, near, and dearly loved. Benjamin is called "the beloved of the Lord," resting secure in God's protection all day long.

Let this image wash over you. God does not merely tolerate His people or keep them at arm's length. He carries them close, shields them all day long, and calls them beloved. There is deep security here — not the security of our own strength, but the security of being held near to the heart of God.

Notice the promise that He "shields him all day long." Not just in the dramatic moments, but through every hour, God's protective care surrounds His beloved. From morning to night, we rest in His keeping.

This is the inheritance of everyone who belongs to God through Christ. You are the beloved of the Lord. Jesus is the Good Shepherd who carries the lamb close (Luke 15:5), and He calls you His own. When you feel weak, afraid, or unsteady, remember where you rest — between the shoulders of the God who loves you and shields you all day long. You are carried, you are close, and you are dearly loved.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I truly see myself as "the beloved of the Lord"?
2. How does the image of resting close to God comfort me?
3. Where do I need to let God carry me rather than striving on my own?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that I am Your beloved, carried close and shielded all day long. When I feel weak or afraid, help me rest between Your shoulders, secure in Your love. Carry me, Lord, close to Your heart. Amen.
